answer.label: In short
answer.lead: D2C fashion and apparel marketing is the work of turning browsing into profitable orders in a category with heavy discounting, size-driven returns and fast creative fatigue. It combines catalogue ads, a steady flow of tested creative, size help on product pages and drops planned around contribution margin.
answer.hl: size-driven returns and fast creative fatigue
answer.who: Monday Marketing Company (MMC) markets D2C fashion and apparel brands in India across creative, Meta and Google, product pages and retention.

answer.chip: Margin after returns, not just sales

paras: Fashion shoppers browse many options, compare on price and look, and are strongly influenced by creators and social feeds. Many order more than one size and return the rest, and cash on delivery brings its own returns.
Because looks go in and out of fashion fast, creative also tires quickly and needs a steady refresh.
blocks.cap: Illustrative scene: shortlisting creators for a fashion drop.

blocks.h: The problem that keeps coming back
paras: Returns and discounts quietly eat margin. A campaign can look strong on ROAS while contribution margin after returns is thin.
We measure margin after returns, test creative on a schedule and read the numbers with the guides and free tools.

callout.title: Size is a marketing problem.
callout.text: Clear size help and honest imagery are some of the cheapest ways to lower returns.

leaks.lede: Each stage below is where a fashion brand loses margin, and the work that fixes it.

stages.breaks: Running the same ad until it tires.
stages.why: Fashion feeds move fast and fatigue sets in quickly.
stages.does: We run a test-and-refresh loop with new hooks, formats and creators. See Meta Ads.

stages.why: Fit and style on a real body persuade more than reach.
stages.does: We shortlist creators for fit, audience and style, with clear terms. See influencer marketing.

stages.breaks: Promoting a handful of hero items.
stages.why: Large ranges need feeds and structure so ads show the right item.
stages.does: We set up catalogues, feeds and dynamic ads. See Google Ads.

stages.breaks: Product pages with thin size information.
stages.why: Wrong-size orders are a main source of returns.
stages.does: We improve size guides, imagery and fit notes. See CRO.

stages.why: Gross ROAS ignores returns and discounts.
stages.does: We report contribution margin after returns and build retention flows. See retention.
